summary: CM550's 10 ms J1939 task list and its datalink control bookkeeping. The even frame task set 0x1b4d8 calls the receive dispatcher (0x212b2), the datalink powertrain control timeout runner (0x23244) and the J1939 monitor (0x22070); the odd frame task set 0x1b504 calls the retarder shift assist end (0x2142c), the periodic transmit queue runner (0x1ff38) and the ignored request countdown (0x23920). The 'ROM table' at 0x1b4da-0x1b4e9 is not a table: the three stored addresses are the operands of the first three jsr (xxx).l instructions of the task set 0x1b4d8 (4eb9 000212b2 / 4eb9 00023244 / 4eb9 00022070), which executiveFrameInterruptHandler calls with bsr.w from 20 places, every second 5 ms frame. CM848 runs the same list in the same order from cm848_phase_group_a_processing. Fourteen functions are step-for-step twins of CM848 functions (the J1939 monitor's three, the write-by-parameter-ID services with their worker and registrar, both retarder request enders, the control device lookup, two ignored request list helpers); the others are counterparts with other code, and the J1922 monitor (0x1fdc0 / 0x1fd6c) has no CM848 code at all. The engine control state is shared by J1939 TSC1 requests and J1922 commands (network type 1 / 0); nothing in this family arbitrates fueling, counts message types or keeps a run time histogram.

functions.role: With the J1922 monitor enabled it records one ended datalink control period of the given control mode (1 speed / 2 torque / 3 limit) in the J1922 monitor's records: it adds 1 to the total count and to that mode's count and stamps key_on_hour_meter into that mode's time and the last control time.
functions.discriminator: It is the only writer (the clear routine 0x1fd6c aside) of the e2m 1101 JC22* records 0x804164-0x80417b, picked by its control mode argument, and it reads the J1922 monitor enable bit 0x80 - not the J1939 monitor bit 0x800 that the session tracker 0x22070 reads.
functions.plate_comment: Records one J1922 control occurrence for the J1922 monitor (algorithm_enable_flags_2_cal.j1922_monitor_enable, e2m JC22MRSW): for control mode 1 (speed) / 2 (torque) / 3 (limit) it adds 1 to the total count 0x804164 (e2m 1101 JC22CU) and to the mode's count (JC22RPCU 0x804170 / JC22TQCU 0x804176 / JC22LMCU 0x80416a) and stores key_on_hour_meter in the mode's time (JC22RPTM / JC22TQTM / JC22LMTM) and in the last control time 0x804166 (JC22TM); any other mode does nothing. Called with the mode that ends: by cm550_runJ1939PowertrainControlTimeouts when the request changes while the previous network type was 0 (J1922), and by cm550_resetEngineTsc1Request when a request times out or reaches its time limit - that call has no network type test, so a J1939 request that ends this way is counted too. CM848 has no counterpart: its j1922_monitor_enable has no reader (was cm550_j1939MessageTypeCounter; PR #53 round 93)

functions.role: Runs the two J1939 periodic transmit queues once per 10 ms tick: for every entry whose next tick equals the queue's tick it adds the entry's interval to the next tick and calls the entry's message builder, then advances the queue's tick.
functions.discriminator: The only code that walks the entry tables 0x80096e / 0x800a36 and calls their handler pointers; the other reader of the J1939 communication enable bit (0x212b2) drains the receive ring. Each queue also needs its bit of the broadcast enable word 0x80aa12 (bit 2 engine / bit 3 retarder).
functions.plate_comment: The 10 ms J1939 periodic transmit scheduler, the second call of the odd frame task set 0x1b504 (every second 5 ms executive frame). With algorithm_enable_flags_11_cal.j1939_communication_enable set it runs queue 0 (the engine node's broadcasts: up to 20 entries of 10 bytes at 0x80096e, count 0x800a9a, tick 0x800a9c) while bit 2 of the broadcast enable word 0x80aa12 is set (e2m JCEGBCEA) and queue 1 (the retarder node's: up to 10 at 0x800a36, count 0x800a9b, tick 0x800a9e) while bit 3 is set (JCRDBCEA): an entry whose next tick equals the queue's tick gets its interval added and its builder called, then the tick counts up. functions.role: Drains the J1939 CAN receive ring within a time budget: for each record it builds the PGN key, drops frames from blocked source addresses and calls the receive handler registered for the key; after a ring overflow it enables the receive interrupts of the J1939 message objects again.
functions.discriminator: The only reader of the receive ring pointers 0x80d9b6 / 0x80d9ba and the only code that scans j1939_receive_handler_table and calls its handlers. It reads the CTM4 time base register 0xfff404 and writes the 82527 message object control bytes at 0xffd810 + 16 n (chip select 4), hence mc68k_.
functions.plate_comment: J1939 receive dispatcher, the first call of the even frame task set 0x1b4d8 (frames 0, 2, ... of the 40-frame executive cycle: every 10 ms). With algorithm_enable_flags_11_cal.j1939_communication_enable set it drains the CAN receive ring (18-byte records, 0x80d72e-0x80d895) for at most 250 CTM4 time base counts: the PGN key is record bytes 1-2 (the PDU specific byte cleared when a PDU1 frame is for the engine's address or 0xFF - for PGN 0 also the retarder's address), byte 3 goes to j1939_received_source_address, a frame whose source is in the blocking table 0x80d9e0 (e2m JCSABLTB) is dropped and otherwise the handler registered in j1939_receive_handler_table is called with the record. After a ring overflow it sets the receive interrupt enable (0xfb) of the 82527 message objects after j1939_transmit_message_object_number again. The counterpart of cm848_dispatchJ1939ReceivedMessages (0x538ef4) (was mc68k_FUN_000212b2; PR #53 round 93)
functions.evidence: 0x212ba move.w (0xfff404),d4 (CTM4_BIUTBR); 0x212c0 andi.w #8 on (0x803caa). Loop test 0x213f8-0x2140c: leave when the time base moved 250 counts (cmpi.l #0xfa / bge); 0x2140e-0x2141e go on while the write pointer 0x80d9b6 differs from the read pointer 0x80d9ba or the overflow byte 0x80d9bf is 1. Body 0x212de: record byte 1 (PDU format) and 2 (PDU specific) into a local key; 0x212ee format 0: specific cleared for the engine address 0x80da01, the retarder address 0x80da0b or 0xff; 0x2131a format below 0xf0: cleared for the engine address or 0xff. 0x2133a record byte 3 -> 0x80d9dc. 0x21344-0x2136a scan the bytes 0x80d9e0-0x80d9e3 (0xfe ends the list); a match sets d2 and skips the handler. 0x21370-0x2139a scan 0x800ab0 (6-byte entries, count byte 0x800b10): cmp.w the key, on a match push the record pointer and jsr ((2,a2)). 0x2139c read pointer + 18, past 0x80d884 back to 0x80d72e. 0x213b0-0x213f6: overflow byte 1 -> cleared, then with interrupts masked (ori.w #0x700,sr) move.b #0xfb to 0xffd810 + 16 x (0x80d9f4) for the objects up to (0x80d9f6); 0xfb sets RXIE in an 82527 message object's control 0 byte.
